ko.title: 3%를 향한 질주: 일본, 영국, 독일을 뒤흔드는 글로벌 채권 매도세의 내부

segments.src: ## A Quiet Corner of Finance Suddenly Isn't Quiet
segments.tr: ## 금융권의 조용한 구석이 갑자기 조용하지 않다

segments.src: Government bonds are usually the sleepy end of the financial markets — the place investors go when they want safety, not drama.
segments.tr: 국채는 보통 금융 시장에서 가장 조용한 분야이며, 투자자들이 드라마가 아닌 안전을 원할 때 찾는 곳입니다.

segments.src: That reputation is being tested.
segments.tr: 그 명성이 시험대에 올랐습니다.

segments.src: In recent sessions, a synchronized selloff has pushed borrowing costs higher across some of the world's largest economies, and the moves are big enough that they're spilling over into headlines usually reserved for stocks or crypto.
segments.tr: 최근 세션에서 동시다발적인 매도세로 인해 세계 최대 경제국들의 차입 비용이 상승했으며, 이 움직임은 주식이나 암호화폐에 주로 할애되던 헤드라인을 장식할 정도로 큽니다.

segments.src: In the United States, the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note has climbed to its highest level since 2023.
segments.tr: 미국에서는 10년 만기 기준 국채 금리가 2023년 이후 최고 수준으로 올랐습니다.

segments.src: In Japan, the 10-year government bond yield has pushed past 3% for the first time in roughly three decades — a level that would have seemed almost unthinkable during the country's long stretch of near-zero and even negative interest rates.
segments.tr: 일본에서는 10년 만기 국채 금리가 약 3 thập기(30년) 만에 처음으로 3%를 넘어섰는데, 이는 제로 금리 및 마이너스 금리가 장기화되던 시기에는 거의 상상하기 어려웠던 수준입니다.

segments.src: Yields on UK gilts and German bunds have also risen sharply, adding the world's other major bond markets to the list.
segments.tr: 영국 길트채와 독일 분드채의 금리도 급등하여 세계의 다른 주요 채권 시장들이 명단에 추가되었습니다.

segments.src: ## Why Bond Yields Matter Even If You've Never Bought One
segments.tr: ## 채권 금리를 한 번도 사지 않은 사람에게도 중요한 이유

segments.src: When a government's bond yield rises, it simply means investors are demanding a higher return to lend that government money.
segments.tr: 정부의 채권 금리가 상승한다는 것은 단순히 투자자들이 해당 정부에 돈을 빌려주는 대가로 더 높은 수익률을 요구하고 있음을 의미합니다.

segments.src: But the ripple effects reach far beyond national treasuries.
segments.tr: 그러나 그 파급 효과는 국가 재정을 훨씬 넘어섭니다.

segments.src: Mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs, and even the interest charged on car loans and credit cards tend to track government bond yields over time.
segments.tr: 모기지 금리, 기업 차입 비용, 자동차 대출 및 신용카드의 이자까지 시간이 지남에 따라 국채 금리를 따르는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: Higher sovereign yields generally translate into a more expensive cost of credit throughout the economy, which is why moves like this are being watched so closely by businesses and households alike, not just professional traders.
segments.tr: 국채 금리가 높아지면 일반적으로 경제 전반의 신용 비용이 더 비싸지며, 이것이 바로 이러한 움직임을 전문 트레이더뿐만 아니라 기업과 가계 모두가 그토록 면밀히 주시하고 있는 이유입니다.

segments.src: ## What's Driving the Selloff
segments.tr: ## 매도세를 주도하는 요인

segments.src: Market participants point to a mix of overlapping forces rather than a single cause.
segments.tr: 시장 참여자들은 단일 원인보다는 중첩된 세력의 조합을 지적합니다.

segments.src: **Oil and the Middle East.** Ongoing tensions in the Middle East have kept energy markets on edge, and analysts say the risk of sustained higher oil prices is feeding directly into inflation expectations.
segments.tr: **석유와 중동.** 중동의 지속되는 긴장으로 인해 에너지 시장은 긴장 상태를 유지하고 있으며, 분석가들은 지속적으로 높은 유가의 위험이 인플레이션 기대치에 직접적으로 반영되고 있다고 말합니다.

segments.src: Energy costs flow into nearly everything — transportation, manufacturing, heating — so persistent oil-price pressure tends to push broader inflation forecasts higher.
segments.tr: 에너지 비용은 운송, 제조업, 난방 등 거의 모든 것에 유입되므로 지속적인 유가 압력은 광범위한 인플레이션 전망을 높이는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: **A shift toward protectionism.** Many economists argue that a broader global move toward tariffs and trade barriers is structurally different from the low-inflation, hyper-globalized era of the 2010s.
segments.tr: **보호무역주의로의 전환.** 많은 경제학자들은 관세와 무역 장벽을 향한 광범위한 글로벌 움직임이 2010년대의 저인플레이션, 초세계화 시대와는 구조적으로 다르다고 주장합니다.

segments.src: When goods move less freely across borders, they generally cost more to produce and import, which can keep price pressures elevated for longer than markets previously assumed.
segments.tr: 국경을 넘나드는 상품의 이동이 자유롭지 못하면 일반적으로 생산 및 수입 비용이 더 많이 들며, 이는 시장이 이전에 가정했던 것보다 더 오랜 기간 동안 가격 압력을 높게 유지할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: **Fiscal pressures.** In several major economies, government borrowing has stayed elevated even as growth has cooled, adding to the overall supply of bonds that need to find buyers — a dynamic that tends to push yields up when demand doesn't keep pace.
segments.tr: **재정 압박.** 여러 주요 경제국에서 성장이 둔화되었음에도 불구하고 정부 차입은 높은 수준을 유지하여 구매자를 찾아야 하는 채권의 전반적인 공급을 가중시켰으며, 이는 수요가 따라가지 못할 때 금리를 상승시키는 경향이 있는 역학입니다.

segments.src: **Japan's special case.** Japan's move is especially notable because it marks the end of an era.
segments.tr: **일본의 특수한 사례.** 일본의 움직임은 한 시대의 종말을 고한다는 점에서 특히 주목할 만합니다.

segments.src: For decades, ultra-low Japanese yields were treated almost as a fixture of the global financial system, allowing investors worldwide to borrow cheaply in yen and invest elsewhere — the so-called "carry trade."
segments.tr: 수십 년 동안 일본의 초저금리는 글로벌 금융 시스템의 고정 장치처럼 취급되어 전 세계 투자자들이 엔화로 저렴하게 차입하여 다른 곳에 투자할 수 있게 해주었습니다. 이른바 "캐리 트레이드"입니다.

segments.src: A sustained rise above 3% suggests that era may be genuinely over, with implications for how capital is allocated globally.
segments.tr: 3%를 넘는 지속적인 상승은 전 세계적으로 자본이 배분되는 방식에 시사점을 주며 그 시대가 진정으로 끝났음을 시사합니다.

segments.src: ## The Bigger Picture: Are We in a New Inflation Regime?
segments.tr: ## 더 큰 그림: 우리는 새로운 인플레이션 체제에 들어섰는가?

segments.src: The common thread across these explanations is a growing debate about whether the world has entered a "structurally" higher inflation environment — meaning price pressures that are more persistent and harder to bring down than the temporary post-pandemic spike of 2021-2022.
segments.tr: 이러한 설명들의 공통 분모는 세계가 "구조적으로" 더 높은 인플레이션 환경에 진입했는지에 대한 논쟁이 커지고 있다는 점입니다. 즉, 2021-2022년의 일시적인 팬데믹 이후 급등세보다 가격 압력이 더 지속적이고 진정시키기 어렵다는 것을 의미합니다.

segments.src: If investors increasingly believe that inflation will run hotter for longer, they demand higher yields to compensate for the eroding purchasing power of fixed future payments.
segments.tr: 투자자들이 인플레이션이 더 오래 더 뜨겁게 유지될 것이라고 점점 더 믿게 된다면, 미래의 고정 지급액의 구매력 저하를 보상하기 위해 더 높은 수익률을 요구하게 됩니다.

segments.src: That belief, once it takes hold in markets, can become somewhat self-reinforcing.
segments.tr: 그러한 믿음은 일단 시장에 자리를 잡으면 어느 정도 자기 강화적이 될 수 있습니다.

segments.src: It's worth noting that bond markets can be volatile and sentiment-driven in the short term, and yields have moved sharply in both directions before without signaling a permanent regime change.
segments.tr: 채권 시장은 단기적으로 변동성이 크고 심리에 의해 움직일 수 있으며, 영구적인 체제 변화를 알리지 않고도 금리가 양방향으로 급격하게 움직인 적이 있다는 점을 주목할 가치가 있습니다.

segments.src: Central banks in the US, UK, Japan, and the eurozone are all watching these developments closely, and their policy responses in the months ahead will likely play a significant role in whether this selloff stabilizes or continues.
segments.tr: 미국, 영국, 일본, 유로존의 중앙은행들은 이러한 발전 상황을 면밀히 주시하고 있으며, 앞으로 몇 달 동안의 정책 대응은 이번 매도세가 안정될지 아니면 계속될지에 중요한 역할을 할 것입니다.

segments.src: ## What It Means Going Forward
segments.tr: ## 향후 의미하는 바

segments.src: For now, the takeaway for everyday readers is less about any single number and more about the trend: borrowing costs are rising across multiple major economies at the same time, driven by a combination of geopolitical risk, trade policy shifts, and fiscal dynamics.
segments.tr: 현재로서는 일반 독자들을 위한 시사점은 단일 숫자보다는 트렌드에 가깝습니다. 지정학적 위험, 무역 정책 변화, 재정 역학의 조합으로 인해 여러 주요 경제국에서 차입 비용이 동시에 상승하고 있습니다.

segments.src: Whether this proves to be a temporary repricing or the start of a longer-lasting shift in the global cost of money is likely to be one of the defining financial stories to watch in the coming months.
segments.tr: 이것이 일시적인 가격 재조정으로 판명될지 아니면 글로벌 자금 비용의 더 오래 지속되는 변화의 시작이 될지는 다가오는 몇 달 동안 주목해야 할 결정적인 금융 이야기 중 하나가 될 것입니다.

zh.title: 3%与攀升：透视震动日本、英国和德国的全球债券抛售潮

segments.src: ## A Quiet Corner of Finance Suddenly Isn't Quiet
segments.tr: ## 金融界的一个安静角落突然不再安静

segments.src: Government bonds are usually the sleepy end of the financial markets — the place investors go when they want safety, not drama.
segments.tr: 政府债券通常是金融市场中最沉寂的领域——是投资者在追求安全而非戏剧性时去的地方。

segments.src: That reputation is being tested.
segments.tr: 这一声誉正在受到考验。

segments.src: In recent sessions, a synchronized selloff has pushed borrowing costs higher across some of the world's largest economies, and the moves are big enough that they're spilling over into headlines usually reserved for stocks or crypto.
segments.tr: 在最近的交易中，同步的抛售潮推高了全球一些最大经济体的借贷成本，这些波动幅度之大，甚至蔓延到了通常留给股票或加密货币的头条新闻中。

segments.src: In the United States, the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note has climbed to its highest level since 2023.
segments.tr: 在美国，基准10年期国债收益率已攀升至2023年以来的最高水平。

segments.src: In Japan, the 10-year government bond yield has pushed past 3% for the first time in roughly three decades — a level that would have seemed almost unthinkable during the country's long stretch of near-zero and even negative interest rates.
segments.tr: 在日本，10年期国债收益率在大约三十年来首次突破3%——在经历该国长期接近零甚至负利率的时期，这一水平几乎是不可想象的。

segments.src: Yields on UK gilts and German bunds have also risen sharply, adding the world's other major bond markets to the list.
segments.tr: 英国金边债券和德国国债的收益率也急剧上升，使全球其他主要债券市场也加入进来。

segments.src: ## Why Bond Yields Matter Even If You've Never Bought One
segments.tr: ## 为什么即使你从未买过债券，债券收益率也很重要

segments.src: When a government's bond yield rises, it simply means investors are demanding a higher return to lend that government money.
segments.tr: 当政府的债券收益率上升时，这简单意味着投资者要求更高的回报来借给该政府资金。

segments.src: But the ripple effects reach far beyond national treasuries.
segments.tr: 但其涟漪效应远远超出了国家国库。

segments.src: Mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs, and even the interest charged on car loans and credit cards tend to track government bond yields over time.
segments.tr: 随着时间的推移，抵押贷款利率、企业借贷成本，甚至汽车贷款和信用卡的利息往往都会跟随政府债券收益率走势。

segments.src: Higher sovereign yields generally translate into a more expensive cost of credit throughout the economy, which is why moves like this are being watched so closely by businesses and households alike, not just professional traders.
segments.tr: 更高的主权收益率通常意味着整个经济体中信贷成本更高，这就是为什么不仅是专业交易员，企业和家庭也都如此密切关注此类变动的原因。

segments.src: ## What's Driving the Selloff
segments.tr: ## 驱动抛售潮的因素

segments.src: Market participants point to a mix of overlapping forces rather than a single cause.
segments.tr: 市场参与者指出，这是多种重叠力量共同作用的结果，而不是单一原因。

segments.src: **Oil and the Middle East.** Ongoing tensions in the Middle East have kept energy markets on edge, and analysts say the risk of sustained higher oil prices is feeding directly into inflation expectations.
segments.tr: **石油与中东。** 中东持续的紧张局势使能源市场处于紧张状态，分析人士表示，持续高油价的风险正在直接转化为通胀预期。

segments.src: Energy costs flow into nearly everything — transportation, manufacturing, heating — so persistent oil-price pressure tends to push broader inflation forecasts higher.
segments.tr: 能源成本会传导至几乎所有事物——交通、制造、供暖——因此持续的油价压力往往会推高更广泛的通胀预测。

segments.src: **A shift toward protectionism.** Many economists argue that a broader global move toward tariffs and trade barriers is structurally different from the low-inflation, hyper-globalized era of the 2010s.
segments.tr: **向贸易保护主义转变。** 许多经济学家认为，全球更广泛地转向关税和贸易壁垒，在结构上不同于2010年代低通胀、高度全球化的时代。

segments.src: When goods move less freely across borders, they generally cost more to produce and import, which can keep price pressures elevated for longer than markets previously assumed.
segments.tr: 当商品在国与国之间的自由流动减少时，它们的生产和进口成本通常会更高，这可能会使价格压力保持高位的时间长于市场先前的假设。

segments.src: **Fiscal pressures.** In several major economies, government borrowing has stayed elevated even as growth has cooled, adding to the overall supply of bonds that need to find buyers — a dynamic that tends to push yields up when demand doesn't keep pace.
segments.tr: **财政压力。** 在几个主要经济体中，尽管增长放冷，政府借款仍然居高不下，这增加了需要寻找买家的债券总供给——当需求跟不上时，这种动态往往会推高收益率。

segments.src: **Japan's special case.** Japan's move is especially notable because it marks the end of an era.
segments.tr: **日本的特殊案例。** 日本的举动尤为引人注目，因为它标志着一个时代的结束。

segments.src: For decades, ultra-low Japanese yields were treated almost as a fixture of the global financial system, allowing investors worldwide to borrow cheaply in yen and invest elsewhere — the so-called "carry trade."
segments.tr: 几十年来，极低的日本收益率几乎被视为全球金融体系的一个固定部分，允许全球投资者以日元低成本借款并投资于其他地方——即所谓的“套利交易”。

segments.src: A sustained rise above 3% suggests that era may be genuinely over, with implications for how capital is allocated globally.
segments.tr: 持续升至3%以上表明这个时代可能真的已经结束，这对全球资本配置产生了影响。

segments.src: ## The Bigger Picture: Are We in a New Inflation Regime?
segments.tr: ## 更宏大的图景：我们是否处于一个新的通胀体制中？

segments.src: The common thread across these explanations is a growing debate about whether the world has entered a "structurally" higher inflation environment — meaning price pressures that are more persistent and harder to bring down than the temporary post-pandemic spike of 2021-2022.
segments.tr: 这些解释背后的共同线索是一个日益激烈的辩论：世界是否已经进入了一个“结构性”更高的通胀环境——这意味着价格压力比2021-2022年大流行后的暂时飙升更持久、更难打压。

segments.src: If investors increasingly believe that inflation will run hotter for longer, they demand higher yields to compensate for the eroding purchasing power of fixed future payments.
segments.tr: 如果投资者越来越相信通胀将持续更长时间、更高水平，他们就会要求更高的收益率，以弥补未来固定支付购买力的侵蚀。

segments.src: That belief, once it takes hold in markets, can become somewhat self-reinforcing.
segments.tr: 一旦这种信念在市场中站稳脚跟，它就会变得有点自我强化。

segments.src: It's worth noting that bond markets can be volatile and sentiment-driven in the short term, and yields have moved sharply in both directions before without signaling a permanent regime change.
segments.tr: 值得注意的是，在短期内，债券市场可能是动荡且受情绪驱动的，收益率以前曾在两个方向上大幅波动，而并未预示着永久性的体制转变。

segments.src: Central banks in the US, UK, Japan, and the eurozone are all watching these developments closely, and their policy responses in the months ahead will likely play a significant role in whether this selloff stabilizes or continues.
segments.tr: 美国、英国、日本和欧元区的央行都在密切关注这些事态发展，他们在未来几个月的政策回应可能会在这次抛售是趋于稳定还是继续方面发挥重要作用。

segments.src: ## What It Means Going Forward
segments.tr: ## 前景意味着什么

segments.src: For now, the takeaway for everyday readers is less about any single number and more about the trend: borrowing costs are rising across multiple major economies at the same time, driven by a combination of geopolitical risk, trade policy shifts, and fiscal dynamics.
segments.tr: 目前，普通读者带走的启示与其说是一个单一数字，不如说是这一趋势：由地缘政治风险、贸易政策转变和财政动态共同驱动，多个主要经济体的借贷成本正在同时上升。

segments.src: Whether this proves to be a temporary repricing or the start of a longer-lasting shift in the global cost of money is likely to be one of the defining financial stories to watch in the coming months.

segments.src: ## A Quiet Corner of Finance Suddenly Isn't Quiet
segments.tr: ## वित्त का एक शांत कोना अचानक शांत नहीं रहा

segments.tr: सरकारी बॉन्ड आमतौर पर वित्तीय बाजारों का सुस्त हिस्सा होते हैं — वह जगह जहाँ निवेशक तब जाते हैं जब उन्हें सुरक्षा चाहिए होती है, न कि ड्रामा।

segments.src: That reputation is being tested.
segments.tr: उस प्रतिष्ठा की परीक्षा ली जा रही है।

segments.src: In recent sessions, a synchronized selloff has pushed borrowing costs higher across some of the world's largest economies, and the moves are big enough that they're spilling over into headlines usually reserved for stocks or crypto.
segments.tr: हाल के सत्रों में, एक समन्वित बिकवाली ने दुनिया की कुछ सबसे बड़ी अर्थव्यवस्थाओं में उधार लेने की लागत को बढ़ा दिया है, और ये कदम इतने बड़े हैं कि वे उन सुर्खियों में भी जगह बना रहे हैं जो आमतौर पर शेयरों या क्रिप्टो के लिए आरक्षित होती हैं।

segments.src: In the United States, the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note has climbed to its highest level since 2023.
segments.tr: संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका में, बेंचमार्क 10-वर्षीय ट्रेजरी नोट पर यील्ड 2023 के बाद से अपने उच्चतम स्तर पर पहुंच गई है।

segments.src: In Japan, the 10-year government bond yield has pushed past 3% for the first time in roughly three decades — a level that would have seemed almost unthinkable during the country's long stretch of near-zero and even negative interest rates.

segments.src: Yields on UK gilts and German bunds have also risen sharply, adding the world's other major bond markets to the list.
segments.tr: यूके गिल्ट्स (UK gilts) और जर्मन बंड्स (German bunds) पर यील्ड में भी तेजी से वृद्धि हुई है, जिससे दुनिया के अन्य प्रमुख बॉन्ड बाजार भी इस सूची में शामिल हो गए हैं।

segments.src: ## Why Bond Yields Matter Even If You've Never Bought One
segments.tr: ## बॉन्ड यील्ड क्यों मायने रखती है, भले ही आपने कभी कोई बॉन्ड न खरीदा हो

segments.src: When a government's bond yield rises, it simply means investors are demanding a higher return to lend that government money.
segments.tr: जब किसी सरकार की बॉन्ड यील्ड बढ़ती है, तो इसका सीधा सा मतलब है कि निवेशक उस सरकार को पैसा उधार देने के लिए अधिक रिटर्न की मांग कर रहे हैं।

segments.src: But the ripple effects reach far beyond national treasuries.
segments.tr: लेकिन इसके प्रभाव राष्ट्रीय खजाने से कहीं आगे तक जाते हैं।

segments.src: Mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs, and even the interest charged on car loans and credit cards tend to track government bond yields over time.
segments.tr: मॉर्गेज दरें, कॉर्पोरेट उधार लेने की लागत, और यहां तक कि कार ऋण और क्रेडिट कार्ड पर ली जाने वाली ब्याज दरें भी समय के साथ सरकारी बॉन्ड यील्ड का अनुसरण करती हैं।

segments.src: Higher sovereign yields generally translate into a more expensive cost of credit throughout the economy, which is why moves like this are being watched so closely by businesses and households alike, not just professional traders.
segments.tr: उच्च संप्रभु यील्ड का मतलब आमतौर पर पूरी अर्थव्यवस्था में क्रेडिट की महंगी लागत होता है, यही कारण है कि इस तरह के कदमों पर न केवल पेशेवर व्यापारियों द्वारा, बल्कि व्यवसायों और परिवारों द्वारा भी इतनी बारीकी से नजर रखी जा रही है।

segments.src: ## What's Driving the Selloff
segments.tr: ## बिकवाली का कारण क्या है

segments.src: Market participants point to a mix of overlapping forces rather than a single cause.
segments.tr: बाजार के प्रतिभागी किसी एक कारण के बजाय परस्पर जुड़ी ताकतों के मिश्रण की ओर इशारा करते हैं।

segments.src: **Oil and the Middle East.** Ongoing tensions in the Middle East have kept energy markets on edge, and analysts say the risk of sustained higher oil prices is feeding directly into inflation expectations.
segments.tr: **तेल और मध्य पूर्व।** मध्य पूर्व में जारी तनाव ने ऊर्जा बाजारों को तनाव में रखा है, और विश्लेषकों का कहना है कि लंबे समय तक उच्च तेल कीमतों का जोखिम सीधे तौर पर मुद्रास्फीति की उम्मीदों को प्रभावित कर रहा है।

segments.src: Energy costs flow into nearly everything — transportation, manufacturing, heating — so persistent oil-price pressure tends to push broader inflation forecasts higher.
segments.tr: ऊर्जा की लागत लगभग हर चीज में प्रवाहित होती है — परिवहन, विनिर्माण, हीटिंग — इसलिए तेल की कीमतों का लगातार दबाव व्यापक मुद्रास्फीति के पूर्वानुमानों को ऊपर की ओर धकेलता है।

segments.src: **A shift toward protectionism.** Many economists argue that a broader global move toward tariffs and trade barriers is structurally different from the low-inflation, hyper-globalized era of the 2010s.
segments.tr: **संरक्षणवाद की ओर एक बदलाव।** कई अर्थशास्त्री तर्क देते हैं कि टैरिफ और व्यापार बाधाओं की ओर एक व्यापक वैश्विक कदम 2010 के दशक के कम-मुद्रास्फीति, अति-वैश्वीकृत युग से संरचनात्मक रूप से अलग है।

segments.src: When goods move less freely across borders, they generally cost more to produce and import, which can keep price pressures elevated for longer than markets previously assumed.
segments.tr: जब सामान सीमाओं के पार कम स्वतंत्र रूप से चलता है, तो उन्हें उत्पादित करने और आयात करने में आमतौर पर अधिक लागत आती है, जो बाजारों द्वारा पहले सोचे गए समय से अधिक समय तक मूल्य दबाव को ऊंचा रख सकता है।

segments.src: **Fiscal pressures.** In several major economies, government borrowing has stayed elevated even as growth has cooled, adding to the overall supply of bonds that need to find buyers — a dynamic that tends to push yields up when demand doesn't keep pace.
segments.tr: **राजकोषीय दबाव।** कई प्रमुख अर्थव्यवस्थाओं में, विकास धीमा होने के बावजूद सरकारी उधार का स्तर ऊंचा बना हुआ है, जिससे बॉन्ड की कुल आपूर्ति बढ़ रही है जिन्हें खरीदारों की आवश्यकता है — एक ऐसी गतिशीलता जो मांग के साथ तालमेल न बिठा पाने पर यील्ड को ऊपर की ओर धकेलती है।

segments.src: **Japan's special case.** Japan's move is especially notable because it marks the end of an era.
segments.tr: **जापान का विशेष मामला।** जापान का कदम विशेष रूप से उल्लेखनीय है क्योंकि यह एक युग के अंत का प्रतीक है।

segments.src: For decades, ultra-low Japanese yields were treated almost as a fixture of the global financial system, allowing investors worldwide to borrow cheaply in yen and invest elsewhere — the so-called "carry trade."
segments.tr: दशकों से, अल्ट्रा-लो जापानी यील्ड को वैश्विक वित्तीय प्रणाली के एक स्थायी हिस्से के रूप में माना जाता था, जिससे दुनिया भर के निवेशकों को येन में सस्ते में उधार लेने और कहीं और निवेश करने की अनुमति मिलती थी — जिसे "कैरी ट्रेड" कहा जाता है।

segments.src: A sustained rise above 3% suggests that era may be genuinely over, with implications for how capital is allocated globally.
segments.tr: 3% से ऊपर की निरंतर वृद्धि बताती है कि वह युग वास्तव में समाप्त हो सकता है, जिसके वैश्विक स्तर पर पूंजी के आवंटन के तरीके पर निहितार्थ हैं।

segments.src: ## The Bigger Picture: Are We in a New Inflation Regime?
segments.tr: ## बड़ी तस्वीर: क्या हम एक नई मुद्रास्फीति व्यवस्था में हैं?

segments.src: The common thread across these explanations is a growing debate about whether the world has entered a "structurally" higher inflation environment — meaning price pressures that are more persistent and harder to bring down than the temporary post-pandemic spike of 2021-2022.
segments.tr: इन स्पष्टीकरणों में सामान्य सूत्र इस बात पर बढ़ती बहस है कि क्या दुनिया एक "संरचनात्मक रूप से" उच्च मुद्रास्फीति वाले वातावरण में प्रवेश कर गई है — जिसका अर्थ है मूल्य दबाव जो 2021-2022 की महामारी के बाद की अस्थायी वृद्धि की तुलना में अधिक स्थायी और कम करना कठिन है।

segments.src: If investors increasingly believe that inflation will run hotter for longer, they demand higher yields to compensate for the eroding purchasing power of fixed future payments.
segments.tr: यदि निवेशक तेजी से यह मानते हैं कि मुद्रास्फीति लंबे समय तक अधिक रहेगी, तो वे भविष्य के निश्चित भुगतानों की घटती क्रय शक्ति की भरपाई के लिए उच्च यील्ड की मांग करते हैं।

segments.src: That belief, once it takes hold in markets, can become somewhat self-reinforcing.
segments.tr: वह विश्वास, एक बार जब यह बाजारों में पकड़ बना लेता है, तो कुछ हद तक आत्म-सुदृढ़ीकरण बन सकता है।

segments.src: It's worth noting that bond markets can be volatile and sentiment-driven in the short term, and yields have moved sharply in both directions before without signaling a permanent regime change.
segments.tr: यह ध्यान देने योग्य है कि बॉन्ड बाजार अल्पकालिक रूप से अस्थिर और भावना-संचालित हो सकते हैं, और यील्ड पहले भी स्थायी शासन परिवर्तन का संकेत दिए बिना दोनों दिशाओं में तेजी से आगे बढ़ी हैं।

segments.src: Central banks in the US, UK, Japan, and the eurozone are all watching these developments closely, and their policy responses in the months ahead will likely play a significant role in whether this selloff stabilizes or continues.
segments.tr: अमेरिका, यूके, जापान और यूरोज़ोन के केंद्रीय बैंक इन घटनाक्रमों पर बारीकी से नजर रख रहे हैं, और आने वाले महीनों में उनकी नीतिगत प्रतिक्रियाएं इस बात में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाएंगी कि क्या यह बिकवाली स्थिर होती है या जारी रहती है।

segments.src: ## What It Means Going Forward
segments.tr: ## आगे इसका क्या मतलब है

segments.src: For now, the takeaway for everyday readers is less about any single number and more about the trend: borrowing costs are rising across multiple major economies at the same time, driven by a combination of geopolitical risk, trade policy shifts, and fiscal dynamics.
segments.tr: फिलहाल, आम पाठकों के लिए निष्कर्ष किसी एक संख्या के बारे में कम और रुझान के बारे में अधिक है: भू-राजनीतिक जोखिम, व्यापार नीति में बदलाव और राजकोषीय गतिशीलता के संयोजन से प्रेरित होकर, कई प्रमुख अर्थव्यवस्थाओं में उधार लेने की लागत एक ही समय में बढ़ रही है।

segments.src: Whether this proves to be a temporary repricing or the start of a longer-lasting shift in the global cost of money is likely to be one of the defining financial stories to watch in the coming months.
segments.tr: क्या यह एक अस्थायी पुनर्मूल्यांकन साबित होता है या वैश्विक मुद्रा लागत में लंबे समय तक चलने वाले बदलाव की शुरुआत है, यह आने वाले महीनों में देखने के लिए सबसे महत्वपूर्ण वित्तीय कहानियों में से एक होने की संभावना है।

es.title: 3% y subiendo: Dentro de la venta masiva de bonos globales que sacude a Japón, Gran Bretaña y Alemania

segments.src: ## A Quiet Corner of Finance Suddenly Isn't Quiet
segments.tr: ## Un rincón tranquilo de las finanzas de repente deja de estarlo

segments.src: Government bonds are usually the sleepy end of the financial markets — the place investors go when they want safety, not drama.
segments.tr: Los bonos gubernamentales suelen ser el sector más aletargado de los mercados financieros, el lugar al que acuden los inversores cuando buscan seguridad, no drama.

segments.src: That reputation is being tested.
segments.tr: Esa reputación se está poniendo a prueba.

segments.src: In recent sessions, a synchronized selloff has pushed borrowing costs higher across some of the world's largest economies, and the moves are big enough that they're spilling over into headlines usually reserved for stocks or crypto.
segments.tr: En las últimas sesiones, una venta masiva sincronizada ha elevado los costos de endeudamiento en algunas de las economías más grandes del mundo, y los movimientos son lo suficientemente grandes como para saltar a los titulares que habitualmente se reservan para las acciones o las criptomonedas.

segments.src: In the United States, the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note has climbed to its highest level since 2023.
segments.tr: In Estados Unidos, el rendimiento del bono del Tesoro a 10 años de referencia ha subido a su nivel más alto desde 2023.

segments.src: In Japan, the 10-year government bond yield has pushed past 3% for the first time in roughly three decades — a level that would have seemed almost unthinkable during the country's long stretch of near-zero and even negative interest rates.
segments.tr: En Japón, el rendimiento del bono gubernamental a 10 años ha superado el 3% por primera vez en aproximadamente tres décadas, un nivel que habría parecido casi impensable durante el largo período de tasas de interés cercanas a cero e incluso negativas del país.

segments.src: Yields on UK gilts and German bunds have also risen sharply, adding the world's other major bond markets to the list.
segments.tr: Los rendimientos de los gilts del Reino Unido y de los bunds alemanes también han subido con fuerza, sumando a los otros mercados de bonos importantes del mundo a la lista.

segments.src: ## Why Bond Yields Matter Even If You've Never Bought One
segments.tr: ## Por qué importan los rendimientos de los bonos incluso si nunca ha comprado uno

segments.src: When a government's bond yield rises, it simply means investors are demanding a higher return to lend that government money.
segments.tr: Cuando el rendimiento del bono de un gobierno sube, simplemente significa que los inversores exigen un mayor retorno para prestar dinero a ese gobierno.

segments.src: But the ripple effects reach far beyond national treasuries.
segments.tr: Pero los efectos dominó van mucho más allá de las tesorerías nacionales.

segments.src: Mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs, and even the interest charged on car loans and credit cards tend to track government bond yields over time.
segments.tr: Las tasas hipotecarias, los costos de endeudamiento corporativo e incluso los intereses cobrados en préstamos para automóviles y tarjetas de crédito tienden a seguir los rendimientos de los bonos gubernamentales a lo largo del tiempo.

segments.src: Higher sovereign yields generally translate into a more expensive cost of credit throughout the economy, which is why moves like this are being watched so closely by businesses and households alike, not just professional traders.
segments.tr: Unos rendimientos soberanos más altos generalmente se traducen en un costo del crédito más caro en toda la economía, razón por la cual movimientos como este son vigilados tan de cerca tanto por empresas como por hogares, no solo por operadores profesionales.

segments.src: ## What's Driving the Selloff
segments.tr: ## Qué está impulsando la venta masiva

segments.src: Market participants point to a mix of overlapping forces rather than a single cause.
segments.tr: Los participantes del mercado apuntan a una combinación de fuerzas superpuestas en lugar de a una sola causa.

segments.src: **Oil and the Middle East.** Ongoing tensions in the Middle East have kept energy markets on edge, and analysts say the risk of sustained higher oil prices is feeding directly into inflation expectations.
segments.tr: **El petróleo y Oriente Medio.** Las tensiones continuas en Oriente Medio han mantenido en vilo a los mercados energéticos, y los analistas señalan que el riesgo de precios del petróleo sostenidamente más altos está alimentando directamente las expectativas de inflación.

segments.src: Energy costs flow into nearly everything — transportation, manufacturing, heating — so persistent oil-price pressure tends to push broader inflation forecasts higher.
segments.tr: Los costos de la energía influyen en casi todo (transporte, fabricación, calefacción), por lo que la presión persistente de los precios del petróleo tiende a elevar los pronósticos de inflación general.

segments.src: **A shift toward protectionism.** Many economists argue that a broader global move toward tariffs and trade barriers is structurally different from the low-inflation, hyper-globalized era of the 2010s.
segments.tr: **Un giro hacia el proteccionismo.** Muchos economistas sostienen que un movimiento global más amplio hacia aranceles y barreras comerciales es estructuralmente diferente de la era de baja inflación e hiperglobalización de la década de 2010.

segments.src: When goods move less freely across borders, they generally cost more to produce and import, which can keep price pressures elevated for longer than markets previously assumed.
segments.tr: Cuando los bienes se mueven con menos libertad a través de las fronteras, generalmente cuesta más producirlos e importarlos, lo que puede mantener elevadas las presiones sobre los precios durante más tiempo de lo que los mercados asumían anteriormente.

segments.src: **Fiscal pressures.** In several major economies, government borrowing has stayed elevated even as growth has cooled, adding to the overall supply of bonds that need to find buyers — a dynamic that tends to push yields up when demand doesn't keep pace.
segments.tr: **Presiones fiscales.** En varias economías importantes, el endeudamiento gubernamental se ha mantenido elevado incluso cuando el crecimiento se ha enfriado, lo que aumenta la oferta general de bonos que necesitan encontrar compradores, una dinámica que tiende a presionar los rendimientos al alza cuando la demanda no mantiene el ritmo.

segments.src: ## A Quiet Corner of Finance Suddenly Isn't Quiet

segments.src: Government bonds are usually the sleepy end of the financial markets — the place investors go when they want safety, not drama.

segments.src: That reputation is being tested.
segments.tr: Essa reputação está sendo testada.

segments.src: In recent sessions, a synchronized selloff has pushed borrowing costs higher across some of the world's largest economies, and the moves are big enough that they're spilling over into headlines usually reserved for stocks or crypto.
segments.tr: Nas sessões recentes, uma liquidação sincronizada impulsionou os custos de empréstimos para cima em algumas das maiores economias do mundo, e os movimentos são grandes o suficiente para transbordar para as manchetes normalmente reservadas para ações ou criptomoedas.

segments.src: In the United States, the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note has climbed to its highest level since 2023.
segments.tr: Nos Estados Unidos, o rendimento da nota de referência do Tesouro de 10 anos subiu para o nível mais alto desde 2023.

segments.src: In Japan, the 10-year government bond yield has pushed past 3% for the first time in roughly three decades — a level that would have seemed almost unthinkable during the country's long stretch of near-zero and even negative interest rates.
segments.tr: No Japão, o rendimento dos títulos do governo de 10 anos ultrapassou 3% pela primeira vez em cerca de três décadas — um nível que pareceria quase impensável durante o longo período de taxas de juros próximas de zero e até negativas do país.

segments.src: Yields on UK gilts and German bunds have also risen sharply, adding the world's other major bond markets to the list.
segments.tr: Os rendimentos dos gilts do Reino Unido e dos bunds da Alemanha também subiram acentuadamente, adicionando os outros principais mercados de títulos do mundo à lista.

segments.src: ## Why Bond Yields Matter Even If You've Never Bought One
segments.tr: ## Por Que os Rendimentos dos Títulos Importam Mesmo Que Você Nunca Tenha Comprado Um

segments.src: When a government's bond yield rises, it simply means investors are demanding a higher return to lend that government money.
segments.tr: Quando o rendimento do título de um governo sobe, significa simplesmente que os investidores estão exigindo um retorno maior para emprestar dinheiro a esse governo.

segments.src: But the ripple effects reach far beyond national treasuries.
segments.tr: Mas os efeitos cascata vão muito além dos tesouros nacionais.

segments.src: Mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs, and even the interest charged on car loans and credit cards tend to track government bond yields over time.
segments.tr: As taxas de hipotecas, os custos de empréstimos corporativos e até os juros cobrados em financiamentos de automóveis e cartões de crédito tendem a acompanhar os rendimentos dos títulos do governo ao longo do tempo.

segments.src: Higher sovereign yields generally translate into a more expensive cost of credit throughout the economy, which is why moves like this are being watched so closely by businesses and households alike, not just professional traders.
segments.tr: Rendimentos soberanos mais altos geralmente se traduzem em um custo de crédito mais caro em toda a economia, e é por isso que movimentos como esse estão sendo observados de perto por empresas e famílias, e não apenas por operadores profissionais.

segments.src: ## What's Driving the Selloff
segments.tr: ## O Que Está Impulsionando a Liquidação

segments.src: Market participants point to a mix of overlapping forces rather than a single cause.
segments.tr: Os participantes do mercado apontam para uma combinação de forças sobrepostas, em vez de uma causa única.

segments.src: **Oil and the Middle East.** Ongoing tensions in the Middle East have kept energy markets on edge, and analysts say the risk of sustained higher oil prices is feeding directly into inflation expectations.
segments.tr: **Petróleo e o Oriente Médio.** As tensões contínuas no Oriente Médio mantiveram os mercados de energia apreensivos, e analistas dizem que o risco de preços de petróleo sustentadamente mais altos está alimentando diretamente as expectativas de inflação.

segments.src: Energy costs flow into nearly everything — transportation, manufacturing, heating — so persistent oil-price pressure tends to push broader inflation forecasts higher.
segments.tr: Os custos de energia fluem para quase tudo — transporte, manufatura, aquecimento — portanto, a pressão persistente nos preços do petróleo tende a elevar as previsões mais amplas de inflação.

segments.src: **A shift toward protectionism.** Many economists argue that a broader global move toward tariffs and trade barriers is structurally different from the low-inflation, hyper-globalized era of the 2010s.
segments.tr: **Uma mudança em direção ao protecionismo.** Muitos economistas argumentam que um movimento global mais amplo em direção a tarifas e barreiras comerciais é estruturalmente diferente da era de baixa inflação e hiperglobalizada dos anos 2010.

segments.src: When goods move less freely across borders, they generally cost more to produce and import, which can keep price pressures elevated for longer than markets previously assumed.
segments.tr: Quando os bens circulam de forma menos livre pelas fronteiras, eles geralmente custam mais para serem produzidos e importados, o que pode manter as pressões sobre os preços elevadas por mais tempo do que os mercados supunham anteriormente.

segments.src: **Fiscal pressures.** In several major economies, government borrowing has stayed elevated even as growth has cooled, adding to the overall supply of bonds that need to find buyers — a dynamic that tends to push yields up when demand doesn't keep pace.
segments.tr: **Pressões fiscais.** Em várias das principais economias, o endividamento do governo permaneceu elevado mesmo com o esfriamento do crescimento, aumentando a oferta geral de títulos que precisam encontrar compradores — uma dinâmica que tende a impulsionar os rendimentos para cima quando a demanda não acompanha o ritmo.

segments.src: **Japan's special case.** Japan's move is especially notable because it marks the end of an era.
segments.tr: **O caso especial do Japão.** O movimento do Japão é especialmente notável porque marca o fim de uma era.

segments.src: For decades, ultra-low Japanese yields were treated almost as a fixture of the global financial system, allowing investors worldwide to borrow cheaply in yen and invest elsewhere — the so-called "carry trade."
segments.tr: Durante décadas, os rendimentos ultra-baixos do Japão foram tratados quase como uma constante do sistema financeiro global, permitindo que investidores em todo o mundo pegassem emprestado barato em ienes e investissem em outros lugares — o chamado "carry trade".

segments.src: A sustained rise above 3% suggests that era may be genuinely over, with implications for how capital is allocated globally.
segments.tr: Uma alta sustentada acima de 3% sugere que essa era pode ter realmente terminado, com implicações para como o capital é alocado globalmente.

segments.src: ## The Bigger Picture: Are We in a New Inflation Regime?
segments.tr: ## O Quadro Geral: Estamos em um Novo Regime de Inflação?

segments.src: The common thread across these explanations is a growing debate about whether the world has entered a "structurally" higher inflation environment — meaning price pressures that are more persistent and harder to bring down than the temporary post-pandemic spike of 2021-2022.
segments.tr: O elemento comum entre essas explicações é um debate crescente sobre se o mundo entrou em um ambiente de inflação "estruturalmente" mais alta — significando pressões de preços mais persistentes e mais difíceis de reduzir do que o pico temporário pós-pandemia de 2021-2022.

segments.src: If investors increasingly believe that inflation will run hotter for longer, they demand higher yields to compensate for the eroding purchasing power of fixed future payments.
segments.tr: Se os investidores acreditam cada vez mais que a inflação continuará mais alta por mais tempo, eles exigem rendimentos maiores para compensar a erosão do poder de compra dos pagamentos futuros fixos.

segments.src: That belief, once it takes hold in markets, can become somewhat self-reinforcing.

segments.tr: 国債利回りの上昇は、一般的に経済全体における信用のコストが高くなることを意味します。だからこそ、このような動きはプロのトレーダーだけでなく、企業や家庭からも同様に注視されているのです。

segments.src: ## What's Driving the Selloff
segments.tr: ## 何が債券売りを誘発しているのか

segments.src: Market participants point to a mix of overlapping forces rather than a single cause.
segments.tr: 市場関係者は、単一の原因ではなく、重なり合う複数の要因が絡み合っていると指摘しています。

segments.src: **Oil and the Middle East.** Ongoing tensions in the Middle East have kept energy markets on edge, and analysts say the risk of sustained higher oil prices is feeding directly into inflation expectations.
segments.tr: **原油と中東情勢。** 中東で続く緊張はエネルギー市場を不安定な状態に置いており、アナリストは原油価格の高止まりリスクがインフレ予想に直接影響を与えていると指摘しています。

segments.src: Energy costs flow into nearly everything — transportation, manufacturing, heating — so persistent oil-price pressure tends to push broader inflation forecasts higher.
segments.tr: エネルギーコストは、輸送、製造、暖房など、ほぼすべてのものに波及するため、持続的な原油価格の圧力は、より広範なインフレ予測を押し上げる傾向があります。

segments.src: **A shift toward protectionism.** Many economists argue that a broader global move toward tariffs and trade barriers is structurally different from the low-inflation, hyper-globalized era of the 2010s.
segments.tr: **保護主義へのシフト。** 多くの経済学者は、関税や貿易障壁に向けた世界的な動きは、低インフレで超グローバル化が進んだ2010年代とは構造的に異なると主張しています。

segments.src: When goods move less freely across borders, they generally cost more to produce and import, which can keep price pressures elevated for longer than markets previously assumed.
segments.tr: 国境を越えたモノの移動が制限されると、一般的に生産や輸入のコストが高くなり、市場が以前想定していたよりも長く価格圧力が高い状態が続く可能性があります。

segments.src: **Fiscal pressures.** In several major economies, government borrowing has stayed elevated even as growth has cooled, adding to the overall supply of bonds that need to find buyers — a dynamic that tends to push yields up when demand doesn't keep pace.
segments.tr: **財政圧力。** いくつかの主要経済国では、成長が鈍化しているにもかかわらず政府の借入が高水準を維持しており、買い手を見つける必要のある債券の全体的な供給量が増加しています。これは、需要が追いつかない場合に利回りを押し上げる要因となります。

segments.src: **Japan's special case.** Japan's move is especially notable because it marks the end of an era.
segments.tr: **日本の特殊なケース。** 日本の動きは、一つの時代の終わりを告げるものであるため、特に注目に値します。

segments.src: For decades, ultra-low Japanese yields were treated almost as a fixture of the global financial system, allowing investors worldwide to borrow cheaply in yen and invest elsewhere — the so-called "carry trade."
segments.tr: 何十年もの間、日本の超低金利は世界の金融システムの常識のように扱われ、世界中の投資家が円で安く借りて他国で投資する、いわゆる「キャリートレード」を可能にしていました。

segments.src: A sustained rise above 3% suggests that era may be genuinely over, with implications for how capital is allocated globally.
segments.tr: 3%を上回る水準が持続することは、その時代が本当に終わった可能性を示唆しており、世界的な資本配分のあり方に影響を及ぼします。

segments.src: ## The Bigger Picture: Are We in a New Inflation Regime?
segments.tr: ## 大局的な視点：私たちは新たなインフレ体制にいるのか？

segments.src: The common thread across these explanations is a growing debate about whether the world has entered a "structurally" higher inflation environment — meaning price pressures that are more persistent and harder to bring down than the temporary post-pandemic spike of 2021-2022.
segments.tr: これらの説明に共通する糸口は、世界が「構造的に」高いインフレ環境に入ったのではないかという議論が高まっていることです。つまり、2021年から2022年にかけてのパンデミック後の世界的な一時的急騰よりも、価格圧力が持続し、引き下げることが難しくなっている状態を指します。

segments.src: If investors increasingly believe that inflation will run hotter for longer, they demand higher yields to compensate for the eroding purchasing power of fixed future payments.
segments.tr: インフレがより長く、より高い水準で推移すると投資家が信じるようになれば、将来の固定支払いの購買力低下を補うために、より高い利回りを要求するようになります。

segments.src: That belief, once it takes hold in markets, can become somewhat self-reinforcing.
segments.tr: この信念は、一度市場に定着すると、ある程度自己強化的なものになる可能性があります。

segments.src: It's worth noting that bond markets can be volatile and sentiment-driven in the short term, and yields have moved sharply in both directions before without signaling a permanent regime change.
segments.tr: なお、債券市場は短期的にはボラティリティが高く、センチメントに左右されやすい性質があり、過去にも恒久的な体制変化を示すことなく利回りが両方向に急激に動いたことがある点は留意すべきです。

segments.src: Central banks in the US, UK, Japan, and the eurozone are all watching these developments closely, and their policy responses in the months ahead will likely play a significant role in whether this selloff stabilizes or continues.
segments.tr: 米国、英国、日本、そしてユーロ圏の中央銀行はすべてこれらの動向を注視しており、今後数ヶ月間の政策対応が、この債券売りが沈静化するか、あるいは継続するかを左右する重要な役割を果たすことになるでしょう。

segments.src: ## What It Means Going Forward
segments.tr: ## 今後の展望と意味するもの

segments.src: For now, the takeaway for everyday readers is less about any single number and more about the trend: borrowing costs are rising across multiple major economies at the same time, driven by a combination of geopolitical risk, trade policy shifts, and fiscal dynamics.
segments.tr: 現時点において、一般の読者にとっての要点は、個々の数字そのものよりも、そのトレンドにあります。地政学的リスク、貿易政策の転換、そして財政動向が組み合わさることで、複数の主要経済国で同時に借入コストが上昇しているということです。

segments.src: Whether this proves to be a temporary repricing or the start of a longer-lasting shift in the global cost of money is likely to be one of the defining financial stories to watch in the coming months.
segments.tr: これが一時的な価格再設定（リプライシング）に終わるのか、それとも世界的な資金コストのより長期的な変化の始まりとなるのかは、今後数ヶ月間、注視すべき決定的な金融ニュースの一つとなるでしょう。

segments.src: ## A Quiet Corner of Finance Suddenly Isn't Quiet
segments.tr: ## Eine ruhige Ecke der Finanzwelt ist plötzlich nicht mehr ruhig

segments.src: Government bonds are usually the sleepy end of the financial markets — the place investors go when they want safety, not drama.
segments.tr: Staatsanleihen sind normalerweise der verschlafene Teil der Finanzmärkte – der Ort, an den sich Anleger wenden, wenn sie Sicherheit suchen, nicht Drama.

segments.src: That reputation is being tested.
segments.tr: Dieser Ruf wird derzeit auf die Probe gestellt.

segments.src: In recent sessions, a synchronized selloff has pushed borrowing costs higher across some of the world's largest economies, and the moves are big enough that they're spilling over into headlines usually reserved for stocks or crypto.
segments.tr: In den letzten Sitzungen hat ein synchronisierter Ausverkauf die Kreditkosten in einigen der größten Volkswirtschaften der Welt in die Höhe getrieben, und die Bewegungen sind so groß, dass sie in Schlagzeilen auftauchen, die normalerweise Aktien oder Krypto vorbehalten sind.

segments.src: In the United States, the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note has climbed to its highest level since 2023.
segments.tr: In den Vereinigten Staaten ist die Rendite der 10-jährigen Benchmark-Staatsanleihe auf den höchsten Stand seit 2023 geklettert.

segments.src: In Japan, the 10-year government bond yield has pushed past 3% for the first time in roughly three decades — a level that would have seemed almost unthinkable during the country's long stretch of near-zero and even negative interest rates.
segments.tr: In Japan ist die Rendite 10-jähriger Staatsanleihen zum ersten Mal seit etwa drei Jahrzehnten über 3% gestiegen – ein Niveau, das während der langen Phase der Null- und sogar Negativzinsen des Landes fast undenkbar gewesen wäre.

segments.src: Yields on UK gilts and German bunds have also risen sharply, adding the world's other major bond markets to the list.
segments.tr: Auch die Renditen für britische Gilts und deutsche Bundesanleihen sind stark gestiegen, was die anderen großen Anleihemärkte der Welt auf die Liste setzt.

segments.src: ## Why Bond Yields Matter Even If You've Never Bought One
segments.tr: ## Warum Anleiherenditen wichtig sind, selbst wenn Sie noch nie eine gekauft haben

segments.src: When a government's bond yield rises, it simply means investors are demanding a higher return to lend that government money.
segments.tr: Wenn die Anleiherendite einer Regierung steigt, bedeutet das einfach, dass Anleger eine höhere Rendite verlangen, um dieser Regierung Geld zu leihen.

segments.src: But the ripple effects reach far beyond national treasuries.
segments.tr: Aber die Auswirkungen reichen weit über die nationalen Staatskassen hinaus.

segments.src: Mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs, and even the interest charged on car loans and credit cards tend to track government bond yields over time.
segments.tr: Hypothekenzinsen, Kreditkosten für Unternehmen und sogar die Zinsen für Autokredite und Kreditkarten orientieren sich im Laufe der Zeit tendenziell an den Renditen von Staatsanleihen.

segments.src: Higher sovereign yields generally translate into a more expensive cost of credit throughout the economy, which is why moves like this are being watched so closely by businesses and households alike, not just professional traders.
segments.tr: Höhere Staatsanleiherenditen führen im Allgemeinen zu teureren Kreditkosten in der gesamten Wirtschaft, weshalb solche Bewegungen nicht nur von professionellen Händlern, sondern auch von Unternehmen und Haushalten gleichermaßen so genau beobachtet werden.

segments.src: ## What's Driving the Selloff
segments.tr: ## Was den Ausverkauf antreibt

segments.src: Market participants point to a mix of overlapping forces rather than a single cause.
segments.tr: Marktteilnehmer verweisen auf eine Mischung aus sich überschneidenden Kräften und nicht auf eine einzelne Ursache.

segments.src: **Oil and the Middle East.** Ongoing tensions in the Middle East have kept energy markets on edge, and analysts say the risk of sustained higher oil prices is feeding directly into inflation expectations.
segments.tr: **Öl und der Nahe Osten.** Die anhaltenden Spannungen im Nahen Osten haben die Energiemärkte in Alarmbereitschaft versetzt, und Analysten sagen, dass das Risiko anhaltend höherer Ölpreise direkt in die Inflationserwartungen einfließt.

segments.src: Energy costs flow into nearly everything — transportation, manufacturing, heating — so persistent oil-price pressure tends to push broader inflation forecasts higher.
segments.tr: Energiekosten fließen in fast alles ein – Transport, Fertigung, Heizung –, daher führen anhaltende Ölpreisdrucke tendenziell dazu, dass die allgemeinen Inflationsprognosen steigen.

segments.src: **A shift toward protectionism.** Many economists argue that a broader global move toward tariffs and trade barriers is structurally different from the low-inflation, hyper-globalized era of the 2010s.
segments.tr: **Eine Verschiebung hin zum Protektionismus.** Viele Ökonomen argumentieren, dass eine breitere globale Bewegung hin zu Zöllen und Handelshemmnissen strukturell anders ist als die Ära der niedrigen Inflation und Hyperglobalisierung der 2010er Jahre.

segments.src: When goods move less freely across borders, they generally cost more to produce and import, which can keep price pressures elevated for longer than markets previously assumed.
segments.tr: Wenn Waren sich weniger frei über Grenzen hinweg bewegen, sind sie im Allgemeinen teurer in der Produktion und im Import, was den Preisdruck länger aufrechterhalten kann, als die Märkte zuvor angenommen hatten.

segments.src: **Fiscal pressures.** In several major economies, government borrowing has stayed elevated even as growth has cooled, adding to the overall supply of bonds that need to find buyers — a dynamic that tends to push yields up when demand doesn't keep pace.
segments.tr: **Fiskalischer Druck.** In mehreren großen Volkswirtschaften ist die staatliche Kreditaufnahme hoch geblieben, selbst als das Wachstum nachließ, was das Gesamtangebot an Anleihen erhöht, die Käufer finden müssen – eine Dynamik, die tendenziell die Renditen nach oben treibt, wenn die Nachfrage nicht Schritt hält.

segments.src: **Japan's special case.** Japan's move is especially notable because it marks the end of an era.
segments.tr: **Japans Sonderfall.** Japans Schritt ist besonders bemerkenswert, weil er das Ende einer Ära markiert.

segments.src: For decades, ultra-low Japanese yields were treated almost as a fixture of the global financial system, allowing investors worldwide to borrow cheaply in yen and invest elsewhere — the so-called "carry trade."
segments.tr: Jahrzehntelang wurden extrem niedrige japanische Renditen fast als fester Bestandteil des globalen Finanzsystems behandelt, was es Anlegern weltweit ermöglichte, sich günstig in Yen zu verschulden und anderswo zu investieren – der sogenannte "Carry Trade".

segments.src: A sustained rise above 3% suggests that era may be genuinely over, with implications for how capital is allocated globally.
segments.tr: Ein anhaltender Anstieg über 3% deutet darauf hin, dass diese Ära tatsächlich vorbei sein könnte, mit Auswirkungen darauf, wie Kapital weltweit allokiert wird.

segments.tr: ## Das Gesamtbild: Befinden wir uns in einem neuen Inflationsregime?

segments.tr: Der gemeinsame Nenner dieser Erklärungen ist eine wachsende Debatte darüber, ob die Welt in ein "strukturell" höheres Inflationsumfeld eingetreten ist – was bedeutet, dass der Preisdruck hartnäckiger und schwieriger zu senken ist als der vorübergehende Anstieg nach der Pandemie von 2021-2022.

segments.src: If investors increasingly believe that inflation will run hotter for longer, they demand higher yields to compensate for the eroding purchasing power of fixed future payments.

segments.src: That belief, once it takes hold in markets, can become somewhat self-reinforcing.
segments.tr: Dieser Glaube kann sich, sobald er an den Märkten Fuß gefasst hat, gewissermaßen selbst verstärken.

segments.src: It's worth noting that bond markets can be volatile and sentiment-driven in the short term, and yields have moved sharply in both directions before without signaling a permanent regime change.
segments.tr: Es ist erwähnenswert, dass Anleihemärkte kurzfristig volatil und stimmungsabhängig sein können und die Renditen schon früher stark in beide Richtungen geschwankt sind, ohne einen dauerhaften Regimewechsel zu signalisieren.

segments.tr: Chi phí năng lượng len lỏi vào hầu hết mọi thứ — vận tải, sản xuất, sưởi ấm — vì vậy áp lực giá dầu dai dẳng có xu hướng đẩy các dự báo lạm phát rộng hơn lên cao.

segments.src: **A shift toward protectionism.** Many economists argue that a broader global move toward tariffs and trade barriers is structurally different from the low-inflation, hyper-globalized era of the 2010s.
segments.tr: **Sự chuyển dịch sang chủ nghĩa bảo hộ.** Nhiều nhà kinh tế lập luận rằng xu hướng toàn cầu rộng lớn hơn hướng tới thuế quan và các rào cản thương mại có sự khác biệt về mặt cấu trúc so với kỷ nguyên siêu toàn cầu hóa, lạm phát thấp của những năm 2010.

segments.src: When goods move less freely across borders, they generally cost more to produce and import, which can keep price pressures elevated for longer than markets previously assumed.
segments.tr: Khi hàng hóa lưu thông kém tự do hơn qua biên giới, chúng thường tốn nhiều chi phí hơn để sản xuất và nhập khẩu, điều này có thể giữ cho áp lực giá cả ở mức cao trong thời gian dài hơn so với giả định trước đây của thị trường.

segments.src: **Fiscal pressures.** In several major economies, government borrowing has stayed elevated even as growth has cooled, adding to the overall supply of bonds that need to find buyers — a dynamic that tends to push yields up when demand doesn't keep pace.
segments.tr: **Áp lực tài khóa.** Tại một số nền kinh tế lớn, việc vay nợ của chính phủ vẫn ở mức cao ngay cả khi tăng trưởng đã hạ nhiệt, làm tăng tổng nguồn cung trái phiếu cần tìm người mua — một động lực có xu hướng đẩy lợi suất lên khi nhu cầu không theo kịp.

segments.src: **Japan's special case.** Japan's move is especially notable because it marks the end of an era.
segments.tr: **Trường hợp đặc biệt của Nhật Bản.** Động thái của Nhật Bản đặc biệt đáng chú ý vì nó đánh dấu sự kết thúc của một kỷ nguyên.

segments.src: For decades, ultra-low Japanese yields were treated almost as a fixture of the global financial system, allowing investors worldwide to borrow cheaply in yen and invest elsewhere — the so-called "carry trade."
segments.tr: Trong nhiều thập kỷ, lợi suất cực thấp của Nhật Bản gần như được coi là một đặc điểm cố định của hệ thống tài chính toàn cầu, cho phép các nhà đầu tư trên toàn thế giới vay giá rẻ bằng đồng yên và đầu tư vào nơi khác — cái gọi là "giao dịch chênh lệch lãi suất" (carry trade).

segments.src: A sustained rise above 3% suggests that era may be genuinely over, with implications for how capital is allocated globally.
segments.tr: Việc tăng liên tục trên mức 3% cho thấy kỷ nguyên đó có thể đã thực sự kết thúc, với những tác động đến cách phân bổ vốn trên toàn cầu.

segments.src: ## The Bigger Picture: Are We in a New Inflation Regime?
segments.tr: ## Bức tranh lớn hơn: Chúng ta có đang ở trong một chế độ lạm phát mới?

segments.src: The common thread across these explanations is a growing debate about whether the world has entered a "structurally" higher inflation environment — meaning price pressures that are more persistent and harder to bring down than the temporary post-pandemic spike of 2021-2022.
segments.tr: Sợi chỉ đỏ xuyên suốt các lời giải thích này là cuộc tranh luận ngày càng tăng về việc liệu thế giới đã bước vào một môi trường lạm phát cao hơn "về mặt cấu trúc" hay chưa — nghĩa là áp lực giá cả dai dẳng hơn và khó kéo xuống hơn so với đợt tăng đột biến tạm thời sau đại dịch giai đoạn 2021-2022.

segments.src: If investors increasingly believe that inflation will run hotter for longer, they demand higher yields to compensate for the eroding purchasing power of fixed future payments.
segments.tr: Nếu các nhà đầu tư ngày càng tin rằng lạm phát sẽ nóng hơn trong thời gian dài hơn, họ sẽ yêu cầu lợi suất cao hơn để bù đắp cho sức mua bị xói mòn của các khoản thanh toán cố định trong tương lai.

segments.src: That belief, once it takes hold in markets, can become somewhat self-reinforcing.
segments.tr: Niềm tin đó, một khi đã bám rễ trên thị trường, có thể trở nên tự củng cố ở một mức độ nào đó.

segments.src: It's worth noting that bond markets can be volatile and sentiment-driven in the short term, and yields have moved sharply in both directions before without signaling a permanent regime change.
segments.tr: Cần lưu ý rằng thị trường trái phiếu có thể biến động và bị dẫn dắt bởi tâm lý trong ngắn hạn, và lợi suất từng biến động mạnh theo cả hai hướng trước đây mà không báo hiệu một sự thay đổi chế độ vĩnh viễn.

segments.src: Central banks in the US, UK, Japan, and the eurozone are all watching these developments closely, and their policy responses in the months ahead will likely play a significant role in whether this selloff stabilizes or continues.
segments.tr: Các ngân hàng trung ương ở Mỹ, Anh, Nhật Bản và khu vực đồng euro đều đang theo dõi chặt chẽ những diễn biến này, và các phản ứng chính sách của họ trong những tháng tới có thể sẽ đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc đợt bán tháo này sẽ ổn định hay tiếp tục.

segments.src: ## What It Means Going Forward
segments.tr: ## Điều này có ý nghĩa gì trong thời gian tới

segments.src: For now, the takeaway for everyday readers is less about any single number and more about the trend: borrowing costs are rising across multiple major economies at the same time, driven by a combination of geopolitical risk, trade policy shifts, and fiscal dynamics.
segments.tr: Hiện tại, điều rút ra đối với độc giả thông thường ít liên quan đến bất kỳ con số cụ thể nào mà liên quan nhiều hơn đến xu hướng: chi phí đi vay đang tăng lên ở nhiều nền kinh tế lớn cùng một lúc, được thúc đẩy bởi sự kết hợp của rủi ro địa chính trị, sự thay đổi chính sách thương mại và động lực tài khóa.

segments.src: Whether this proves to be a temporary repricing or the start of a longer-lasting shift in the global cost of money is likely to be one of the defining financial stories to watch in the coming months.
segments.tr: Liệu đây có phải là một đợt định giá lại tạm thời hay là sự khởi đầu của một sự thay đổi lâu dài hơn trong chi phí tiền tệ toàn cầu có thể sẽ là một trong những câu chuyện tài chính định hình đáng chú ý trong những tháng tới.
